newsitem.title: INDIA: India edible oil prices steady on imports.
newsitem.headline: India edible oil prices steady on imports.

text.p: Indian domestic edible oil prices were steady during the week on sustained arrivals of imports but prices may ease further as oilseed sowing picks up, trade officials said on Wednesday.
"Right now prices are more or less steady on sustained import arrivals," said B.V. Mehta, executive director of the Solvent Extractors Association of India.
Mehta said India imported about 724,000 tonnes of edible oil between November 1996 and May 1997, out of which about a total of 250,000 tonnes was sunflower oil from South America.

"If arrival continues at this pace, total imports would be more than 1.5 million tonnes in the whole year," he said. India imported about 1.25 million tonnes of edible oil in the 1995/96 (November-October) season.
Industry officials said demand for Malaysian palm olein in India was currently higher as prices had eased considerably during the past month on expectations of a higher crop.
"Malaysian crop is higher by about 10 percent and it is their peak season coupled with our lean season," Mehta said. "Therefore, a lot of imports (by India) are taking place."
Industry officials said India imported about 85,000 tonnes of edible oil in April and about 166,000 tonnes in May.
"I think imports during the months of June and July would be about 300,000 tonnes," Mehta said.
Traders said groundnut oil was quoted at about 35,800 rupees per tonne and palm olein oil was traded at about 26,500 rupees, the same as last week.
Trade officials said groundnut sowing had started in full swing in the western state of Gujarat after the region received good monsoon showers during the last few days.
"Crop prospects in the western region are good as sowing has started after excellent monsoon rains," said Navinbhai Shah, president of Bombay Oilseeds and Oil Exchange Ltd.

"Prices may further fall if sowing starts in the southern states by next week," he said. The southern states of Karnataka and Andhra Pradesh account for about 35 percent of the country's groundnut output.

Traders said on Tuesday that sowing for the soybean crop of 1997/98 (Nov-Oct) started in the central Indian state of Madhya Pradesh in the past week, after the area received its first monsoon showers.
